radon-monitors.decidedBy: How closely it agrees with a reference radon chamber, whether it reports the long-term average that decisions are made on, and the cost of a result you can act on.

ca: Monitors must be on C-NRPP's list of approved consumer radon monitors, the only independent check of consumer monitors in North America. Its not-approved list has 23 models, many of them recalled by Health Canada.
Kits must be long-term (91 days or more) alpha-track detectors from a C-NRPP-listed maker, with the lab analysis included.
It must report a long-term average, not only today's number: radon swings with the weather, and Health Canada's guideline (200 Bq/m³) applies to the average.
us: Monitors must be on the list of consumer radon monitors approved by Canada's C-NRPP, the only independent check of consumer monitors in North America. Its not-approved list has 23 models, many of them recalled by Health Canada.
Kits must be long-term (90 days or more) detectors with the lab analysis included, from a national radon program.
It must report a long-term average, not only today's number: radon swings with the weather, and EPA's action level (4 pCi/L) is judged on the average.

performance.name: Ecosense RadonEye
performance.why: One of the most consistent consumer monitors in an independent 11-month chamber test, with a fresh reading every 10 minutes: the one to watch what air sealing or a mitigation fan actually did.
facts: On C-NRPP's approved list; stated accuracy ±10% at 370 Bq/m³
New reading every 10 minutes, shown as an hourly rolling average
Plugs in; short- and long-term averages in the free app
performance.price: About $215 at the maker's Canadian store

easy.name: Ecosense EcoQube Flex
easy.why: Runs on batteries, so it moves from the basement to the bedroom, and its always-on screen shows the averages without opening an app.
facts: On C-NRPP's approved list
Two AA batteries: about 2 years with app syncing, up to 7 offline (maker's figures)
E-ink screen with 24-hour to weekly averages and a year of storage
easy.watch: New in late 2025, so there is no long-term drift data yet.

value.name: Long-term alpha-track kit
value.why: The test Health Canada's guidance is written around: three months or more in the lowest lived-in room, then the lab gives you the average you decide on.
facts: Both detectors are C-NRPP-listed
Lab analysis and return postage included in the price
Leave it 91 to 365 days, ideally through the heating season
value.price: $63 for a Radtrak3 at the BC Lung Foundation's shop; kits run about $30 to $65

air-quality-monitors.decidedBy: Which sensors it has (a true NDIR carbon dioxide sensor, particles, radon), whether it shows readings without an app, battery life, and any subscription.
gates: Must measure carbon dioxide and fine particles (PM2.5), or carbon dioxide with a true NDIR sensor: those two numbers answer the ventilation and smoke questions.
Readings on the device itself, no subscription required.
Radon readings count only if the monitor is on C-NRPP's approved list.

performance.name: Airthings View Plus
performance.why: The one monitor that covers the whole house question: radon, fine particles, carbon dioxide and VOCs on one wall-mounted screen.
facts: Its radon readings are on C-NRPP's approved list
Six AA batteries for up to 2 years, or USB-C power
Wi-Fi and Bluetooth; no subscription

sellers.amazon: Airthings View Plus air quality monitor

easy.name: Aranet4 Home
easy.why: The carbon dioxide monitor people leave on the shelf for years: an e-ink screen you read at a glance and batteries that last up to four years.
facts: True NDIR CO₂ sensor, ±(30 ppm + 3%)
Up to 4 years on batteries; readable without the app
No subscription; 2-year warranty
easy.watch: No particle sensor: pair it with the value pick if wildfire smoke reaches you.

value.name: IKEA ALPSTUGA
value.why: Carbon dioxide, fine particles, temperature and humidity on its own screen for the price of a filter: enough to know when to open a window and when smoke has come in.
facts: Shows CO₂, PM2.5, temperature and humidity without an app
Its CO₂ sensor is a cheaper non-NDIR type, rated ±(100 ppm + 10%)
Needs a USB-C power adapter (sold separately); app control needs a Thread hub
value.price: $49.99 at IKEA, plus $9.99 for the power adapter
